properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/18/2025 to OIL & GAS MGMT INC in Parks Township, Armstrong county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OIL & GAS MGMT INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/18/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8249190
Permit API: 005-29119
Unconventional: No
County: Armstrong
Municipality: Parks Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2025
Comments: On Thursday, 9/18/2025, I conducted an inspection of the Oil and Gas Management, Inc. Brown 2 well, permit number 005-29119, due to complaint received 9/16/2025 (CTS #392326). The site is located in the woods off of Chestnut Road in Parks township, Armstrong county. The complaint was submitted as a result of a spill on the site. The spill appears to be used motor oil and I estimated that more than 25 gallons was spilled. This was due to containers (2 - 5 gallon buckets and a 55 gallon drum) and refuse (used oil filter) observed in the immediate area of the spill (see pictures 3, 4, and 5). The operator did not report the spill and it appears that the operator has not visited the site recently. The well was shut in on the day of the inspection, but the operator did report a non-averaged production of 729.0 mcf for the 2024 production (365 days producing, as per OGRE). The well appeared to be disconnected from the compressor (see picture 9) and the compressor does not appear to be functional at this time (no motor, see picture 8). It needs to be noted that the production chart is dated 4-2-23 (see picture 3). The site access road is also in terrible condition. The E and S BMP's have not been maintained and there are multiple areas that are deeply rutted and have significant accelerated erosion.As a result of the site conditions, the operator is being cited for violations to 25 PA Code 78.53, 102.22(a), 102.4(b)(1), 78.57(a), 78.66(b), and CSL 402(b)

Comments: I conducted this inspection in response to a spill that was self reported by Seneca. Seneca discovered three pin holes in the produced water line coming from the E08L pad. Approximately 10'x 20' x3' of soil was impacted by the release of produced water. Jeff Passarello from Seneca estimated that 25 gallons had been released from the compromised line. The leak was found during routine inspection of the line. At the time of my arrival crews had replaced the compromised section of the above ground produced water line and the excavated dirt was placed into 3 short containment boxes. These boxes are being temporarily stored inside of secondary containment on the E08L pad. Field conductivity probes were used to verify the impacted soil had been removed. Conductivity readings throughout the remediated area are comparable to background levels. 30-40 feet of brush was cleared to gain access to the failed section of pipe. A third party contractor was pulling up with a load of mulch and seed to temporarily stabilize the recent earth disturbance while I was on site.All removed soil will be disposed of at an approved facility pending lab results. Comments: Administrative review of documents associated with the plug and skid event of the David Weaver #1 (065-27128) well. Spud of new borehole commenced on 05/28/2026. Operator will be required to submit the information which was omitted in the previous submission. Appropriate Notice of Violations (NOV's) have been documented in this inspection report. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/05/2023 to ARMAC RESOURCES LLC in Warren City, Warren county. 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/05/2023
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8157592
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 9/05/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration case (CTS# 369563). Previously this well was found to have methane detected outside of the well bore and the operator decided to plug the well. Upon completion of their plugging attempt they inadvertently cemented some of their tubing into the well. Subsequently a camera was ran into the well and bubbles were visibly seen at the top of fluid level. A MSA Altair 5X gas meter was used and determined the bubbles were methane being emitted into the well bore. A violation was issued to the operator for not properly plugging the well. To address this violation the operator had a rig attempt to drill down to approx 550', which is 50' below the surface casing shoe and remove the cemented in tubing at which point another camera run would have taken place to see if the well is still bubbling methane. The rig failed to drill down to 550' and it was decided to cement the remaining tubing into the well. Top of cement is now at 288.23' with approx. 102' of tubing encapsulated within the well bore. ARMAC has now contracted Hornburg drilling to attempt to drill and clean out the well-bore to a depth of 550'. While on-site I observed Hornburg Drilling rigging up their equipment. They stated that they anticipate to commence drilling and clean out of the well on 09/06/2023.

Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/30/2024
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8185714
Permit API: 003-22651
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Frazer Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/30/2024
Comments: On April 30, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resource's Drape James Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued: 3/29/23 and expires: 3/28/28) located in Frazer Township, Allegheny County in response to CTS #380249.Nick Reda of Range Resources reportedly noticed on April 30, 2024 at 8:15AM an approximately 84 gallon release of water based drill mud on the graveled well pad in several areas. Nick notified the emergency hotline by 10:02AM and believes there is likely one or more holes in the secondary containment causing fluid to leech out from under the containment.The findings of this inspection are as follows: Upon walking the well pad, orange spray paint markings were made by Nick to designate the affected areas plus some buffer space since it was starting to rain. 7 distinct designated areas were observed, some areas had puddles of fluid in them while other areas had stained gravel. Some puddles were cloudy while others appeared to have a sheen to them. Pooling of fluid with sheen were also seen on the secondary containment in some areas.Conductivity readings were taken inside the different spill areas as well as adjacent to the marked spill areas to determine whether any areas outside of these markings were contaminated as well. A background conductivity reading was taken at the well pad perimeter upslope (0.0159 mS) and the rest of the readings are as follows: inside Spill Area 1: 12.6 mS, outside of Spill Area 1: 0.085 mS, inside of Spill Area 3: 1.529 mS, inside of Spill Area 4: 2.05 mS, outside of Spill Area 4: 0.011 mS, from in a cloudy puddle seen in Spill Area 5: Over Range, outside of Spill Area 5: 0.011 mS, inside Spill Area 6: 1.762 mS, from a sheen puddle seen in Spill Area 7: Over range, and lastly 3 readings were taken in stained sediment around the well pad to see if there were other contaminated areas: 0.042 mS, 0.693 mS and 0.0227 mS. These readings subjugate that a release has in fact occurred, that the areas marked by Nick are the contaminated areas, and that at the time of the inspection the release had not appeared to seep past the visibly marked contaminated areas. The perimeter of the well site on the side of the pad where the release occurred was walked and 2 key way drains were investigated. Both drains were dry and soil conductivity readings were taken at each one (0.091 mS and 0.027 mS). Based on these conductivity readings and the lack of fluid coming from the drains, it does not appear that at this time, the release has seeped down into the drainage system.While onsite, SPSI arrived to begin the remediation process. A skid steer was observed scraping up contaminated gravel into piles, a vacuum truck and 2 clamshell roll off dumpsters were scheduled to arrive today and once they do, the truck will suck up all contaminated fluids and the skid steer will pick up all reachable contaminated gravel/sediment and place it in the dumpsters for disposal. Nick stated that Range was not sure on an exact area in which the release originated from. In theory, Range believes there to be one or more holes/tears in the secondary containment, but none of them have reportedly been discovered at the time of the inspection. Nick stated that the drill rig has two more weeks on site. During these two weeks as equipment is removed and once the drill rig is gone, Range plans to continue inspecting the secondary containment, specifically in areas that currently have equipment on top of it. Any further releases will continue to be cleaned and any holes/tears will be repaired as they are found. The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release and promptly find and repair any holes or tears in the secondary containment to prevent any further releases. The Department also requests the Operator notify the Department of any further releases or impacts that occur and supply the Department with secondary containment inspection reports within 2 business days of receipt of this report.

Comments: On August 12, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resources Conner Samuel well site, located in Cecil Township, Washington County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 8/11/2025 at 8:44pm by Range. Accompanying on today's inspection is Range Resources representative Kevin Rudd.According to the report and Mr. Rudd, after finishing the cement job on the 4H, a flow line became over pressurized due to a valve being left closed. This resulted in a 10 cap dislodging from the flow line and releasing approximately 21 gallons of a synthetic oil based mud (SOBM) fine mist on to the graveled well pad and approximately 42 gallons on to the secondary containment. According to Range, prior to this inspection, the fine mist release was remediated in accordance with 78a66(c)(1) and disposal documents will be provided to the Department upon its receipt.At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 Sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it, and in the on-site mailbox was the Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the well site perimeters were observed to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the release area to be approximately 12ft x 20ft and comprised of had freshly laid gravel. No SOBM was observed on the gravel or on the secondary containment in this area at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the gravel well pad in this release area, and collected soil conductivity readings of 0.0002 mS, in three different locations as well as 0.0651 mS, and 0.0028 mS. These soil conductivity readings are comparable to the background soil conductivity reading of 0.0213 mS, which was collected upslope and adjacent to the well site in a vegetated area.At the time of this inspection, the Department requested Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) for the SOBM involved in the release as well as secondary containment inspection logs. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Rudd provided the Department with the secondary containment logs and attempted to email the Department an electronic copy of the SDSs, however, that email was not received, therefore the Department is again requesting that SDSs for the SOBM be provided to the Department within 2 business days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on observations made at the time of this inspection, it appears that Range remediated the release in accordance with 78a66(c)(1), therefore, violations are noted and immediately corrected.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an app IT error.

Comments: On 8/10/23 at 1201 hrs., I conducted an incident inspection of Madtick Development Corp.'s Musser Associates 2 well site (API 063-32934) in East Mahoning Twp., Indiana Co. The inspection was conducted in response to a phone call received on 8/10/23 from the landowner, indicating that a production fluid release was observed at the well site. The landowner unsuccessfully attempted to contact the operator, and then reported the release to the Department. Upon inspection of the site, stressed/dead vegetation was observed around the production fluid tank onsite, and in an adjacent corn field. A site ID sign is posted, but is illegible and does not display the required information.Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), and 78.66(b) are being cited for failure by the operator to report the release, and are immediately being closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of OGA 3211(G) and OGA 3211(H) are cited for the lack of site ID sign and well tag. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1) are cited for the release of production fluids from the tank onto the ground. The violations will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release anddemonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

Violation ID: 8207456
Permit API: 113-20465
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Cherry Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/12/2024
Comments: Site inspection conducted by EPS Justin Abbott at the Yonkin Well Pad in response to a spill notification submitted by CHK (aka Expand Energy) for a spill detected at 1300 hours on 11/11/24. Meeting on site today with CHK Consultant Brett Fowler. Weather conditions at time of inspection are overcast and 39 degrees F. According to the Emergency Response Notification Report at 1300 hours the following occurred, "up welling of pad adjacent to well head caused concern; Expand started digging at on 11/11/24 at 1:00 p.m.; Expand Energy started digging and encountered produced water with a conductivity of 8000 s/cm. Source of produced water is unknown. Ms. Schaad said that the produced water was not coming up from around the well casing. Expand Energy has Creston Environmental on site utilizing a vac truck to empty excavation. Ms. Schaad said that a small volume of produced water (greater than 5 gallons) has been recovered."At time of inspection, the Department observed a trench dug adjacent to the 5HC well in the affected area. The Department conducted conductivity screenings of the affected area using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Puddled fluid collected in the trench in the affected area was observed with electrical conductivity readings of 3.24 mS/cm. The trenched area of the reported spill was approximately 12' long by 6' wide and 4' deep where water is puddled (photo 4). In a followup conversation with Danielle Schaad, HSE Representative for Chesapeake, the following information was relayed regarding the cause of the spill: the spill of production fluid was observed to be caused by a torn seam in the secondary containment structure which was not apparent until rig mats and containment were removed. Approximately one barrel of fluid was vacuumed from the trench and 14 cubic yards of impacted pad rock were removed from the trench. CHK has contracted with Creston Environmental to pursue Act 2 site characterization. According to Mr. Fowler, Nine Energy Services is conducting wireline operations to change out a valve on the 23HC well (API#113-20465). Plugs have been drilled out, but the wells are shut in and no production equipment has yet been set up on this pad. Rig mats are also observed being stacked and removed from the location at time of inspection. A supersucker vacuum truck is observed on site removing high conductivity fluids from the impacted rock stockpiled in the northwest corner of the pad (photo 5). Comments: On 11/16/22 a follow-up inspection of the McClure 3 OG Well site was conducted related to violations issued on 10/21/22 (IR:3444721). I was accompanied by Chase Ambrose (PA DEP).Background:On 10/21/22, during a routine inspection, violations were issued for a brine release at the McClure 3 OG Well Site. Elevated conductivity was observed inside the earthen containment berm that surrounds the production tank. The tank was in poor condition corroded with rust and holes. Elevated conductivity was also observed outside of the earthen berm containment.An operator response was received by the Department on 11/7/21 stating that the impacted material was removed and disposed of, the well does not produce fluid, and a new tank had been installed. Findings:-Elevated conductivity was observed in soil outside of the containment berm and in standing water inside of the earthen containment berm for the production tank (Photos #1). -The berm appeared to have recently been reworked. The substrate appeared to be uncompacted and no temporary stabilization was observed (Photos #3-4).-A new tank was present. It did not appear to have been connected to the well (Photos #5-6).-The area immediately outside of the earthen berm appeared to have been recently disturbed. No temporary stabilization was observed (Photo #6).-Some discarded pieces of pipe were observed inside the berm (Photo #7).-No outlet or shut off valve was observed for the berm drain (Photo #9).I called Bryan Goletz of Diversified to inform him of my findings. Mr. Goletz stated that he would address the spill and berm. The observed elevated conductivity indicates that the spill has not been fully remediated. Outstanding violations of 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.54 are being issued.

A small erosion channel was observed on the northern cut slope of the pad (photo #3). The DEP recommends repairing the erosion channel to prevent further damage to the slope. All secondary containment structures remain intact and no leaks or other issues were noted today. No new evidence of spills/releases was observed. Violations cited against API #015-23733 on 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time. No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1000 hours.

properties.content:

Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Union Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-10-24
Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to assess conditions after the secondary containment was fully removed from the site. All equipment associated with drilling the wells has been removed from the pad. I met with Tim Moberg of CEC while on location. Mr. Moberg informed me that the northeast corner of the pad had already been excavated and Jen Compton of Rockdale had delineated an area where the electrical conductivity (EC) remained elevated. The EC of two puddles in this area measured around 1.1 mS/cm on my conductivity meter. The puddles on the rest of the pad had EC readings of less than 1.0 mS/cm. According to Mr. Moberg, no excavation had been done in the northeast infiltration basin or in the stormwater channel leading form the northeast corner of the pad to the infiltration basin. In my inspection on 10/21/2019, the EC readings here were all less than 1.0 mS/cm. Mr. Moberg said that they would be taking a number of samples from the pad and the basin but were still developing a sampling plan. Two roll-off boxes were present on the pad. One contained the material excavated from the pad surface. Outstanding violations.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78a and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
Violation ID: 8254150
Permit API: 115-23194
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Springville Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/27/2025
Comments: On site today (09:00) to follow up on the incident that occurred during stimulation operations of the Lauer 12H well on (10/22/25). Met with Operators Drilling and Completions Superintendent (Steve Brominski) to go over operators plans and discuss any pertinent information gathered over the weekend regarding incident. There was no flow witnessed last night (10/26-27/25) with a small return beginning at ~ 06:00 this morning (10/27/25). The flow back was measured at 0.63 bbls (barrels) per hour and continued while I was on site at ~ 0.5 bbls per hour flow rate at the (9x5) annular vent. - Temperature/ Acoustic log was run Friday night (the 24th) into Saturday morning (the 25th). - Dark Vision log was run on Saturday (the 25th). - Lauer 12H (5x9) annulus is open and has been venting since Saturday evening - flow has been dissipating as the annulus approaches static conditions. - On Sunday (the 26th), a cement plug was set on top of kill plugs as an additional barrier. - Dark Vision log is anticipated to be fully processed sometime today (the 27th). Demobilization of equipment began over the weekend and continues today. The on site crane has begun removing pad mats and exposing the containment underneath. Operator will begin removing containment and begin remediation operations beginning tomorrow (10/28/25). Resource GeoTechnical and Environmental Services is on site testing water quality and Moody Labs has begun collecting water samples from surrounding residents. See attached photos for current well head conditions. Coterra's operations team is currently working to finalize a plan for well head replacement.
